title: Learning Humanoid Navigation from Human Data
summary: We present EgoNav, a system that enables a humanoid robot to traverse diverse, unseen environments by learning entirely from 5 hours of human walking data, with no robot data or finetuning. A diffusion model predicts distributions of plausible future trajectories conditioned on past trajectory, a 360 deg visual memory fusing color, depth, and semantics, and video features from a frozen DINOv3 backbone that capture appearance cues invisible to depth sensors. A hybrid sampling scheme achieves real-time inference in 10 denoising steps, and a receding-horizon controller selects paths from the predicted distribution. We validate EgoNav through offline evaluations, where it outperforms baselines in collision avoidance and multi-modal coverage, and through zero-shot deployment on a Unitree G1 humanoid across unseen indoor and outdoor environments. Behaviors such as waiting for doors to open, navigating around crowds, and avoiding glass walls emerge naturally from the learned prior. We will release the dataset and trained models. Our website: https://egonav.weizhuowang.com

AI.tldr: EgoNav is a humanoid robot navigation system that learns from only 5 hours of human walking data using a diffusion model with 360° visual memory (color, depth, semantics, and DINOv3 video features) to predict plausible future trajectories, enabling real-time path planning through unseen indoor and outdoor environments with emergent behaviors like crowd navigation and glass avoidance.
AI.motivation: The authors aim to develop a humanoid robot navigation system that can handle diverse, unseen environments without requiring expensive robot training data or fine-tuning. Traditional navigation systems often require extensive robot-specific data collection and training, which is resource-intensive and time-consuming. The goal is to enable effective robot navigation through human-like learning from human walking data alone.
AI.method: EgoNav combines three key components: (1) A diffusion model that predicts future trajectory distributions conditioned on past trajectory, (2) A 360° visual memory that fuses color, depth, and semantic information along with video features from a frozen DINOv3 backbone to capture appearance cues invisible to depth sensors, and (3) A hybrid sampling scheme achieving real-time inference in 10 denoising steps with a receding-horizon controller that selects paths from the predicted distribution. The entire system is trained on only 5 hours of human walking data without any robot data.
AI.result: EgoNav outperforms baseline systems in offline evaluations regarding collision avoidance and multi-modal coverage. Through zero-shot deployment on a Unitree G1 humanoid robot, it successfully navigates unseen indoor and outdoor environments. Natural behaviors emerge such as waiting for doors to open, navigating around crowds, and avoiding glass walls. The system demonstrates effective navigation without requiring any robot-specific data or fine-tuning.
AI.conclusion: This work demonstrates that humanoid robots can effectively learn navigation behaviors from only 5 hours of human walking data using diffusion models with multi-modal visual perception. The system achieves robust navigation in diverse, unseen environments through zero-shot transfer, suggesting that human walking data alone can provide sufficient prior knowledge for humanoid navigation. The combination of diffusion models, multi-modal visual memory, and efficient inference makes real-time deployment feasible. The released dataset and models enable further research in human-to-robot navigation transfer.

title: Certificate-Driven Closed-Loop Multi-Agent Path Finding with Inheritable Factorization
summary:
Multi-agent coordination in automated warehouses and logistics is commonly modeled as the Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) problem. Closed-loop MAPF algorithms improve scalability by planning only the next movement and replanning online, but this finite-horizon viewpoint can be shortsighted and makes it difficult to preserve global guarantees and exploit compositional structure. This issue is especially visible in Anytime Closed-Loop Conflict-Based Search (ACCBS), which applies Conflict-Based Search (CBS) over dynamically extended finite horizons but, under finite computational budgets, may terminate with short active prefixes in dense instances.
  We introduce certificate trajectories and their associated fleet budget as a general mechanism for filtering closed-loop updates. A certificate provides a conflict-free fallback plan and a monotone upper bound on the remaining cost; accepting only certificate-improving updates yields completeness. The same budget information induces a budget-limited factorization that enables global, inheritable decomposition across timesteps. Instantiating the framework on ACCBS yields Certificate-Driven Conflict-Based Search (CDCBS). Experiments on benchmark maps show that CDCBS achieves more consistent solution quality than ACCBS, particularly in dense settings, while the proposed factorization reduces effective group size.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces certificate trajectories and a fleet budget mechanism to improve closed-loop Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) algorithms. By filtering closed-loop updates using certificate-improving conditions, the authors develop Certificate-Driven Conflict-Based Search (CDCBS), which achieves more consistent solution quality than ACCBS, particularly in dense warehouse environments.
AI.motivation: Closed-loop MAPF algorithms improve scalability by planning only the next movement and replanning online, but their finite-horizon viewpoint is shortsighted and makes it difficult to preserve global guarantees and exploit compositional structure. This limitation is particularly problematic in Anytime Closed-Loop Conflict-Based Search (ACCBS), which applies Conflict-Based Search over dynamically extended finite horizons but may terminate with short active prefixes under finite computational budgets in dense instances.
AI.method: The authors introduce certificate trajectories with associated fleet budgets as a general mechanism for filtering closed-loop updates. A certificate provides a conflict-free fallback plan and a monotone upper bound on remaining cost; accepting only certificate-improving updates yields completeness. The same budget information induces a budget-limited factorization that enables global, inheritable decomposition across timesteps. Instantiating this framework on ACCBS yields Certificate-Driven Conflict-Based Search (CDCBS).
AI.result: Experiments on benchmark maps demonstrate that CDCBS achieves more consistent solution quality than ACCBS, particularly in dense settings. The proposed factorization reduces effective group size, allowing for more efficient planning.
AI.conclusion: Certificate-based approaches with fleet budgets provide a general mechanism for filtering closed-loop updates that maintains completeness while improving solution quality. The CDCBS framework successfully addresses the shortsightedness of finite-horizon planning in closed-loop MAPF algorithms, especially in dense warehouse environments.

title: Reachability-Aware Time Scaling for Path Tracking
summary: This paper studies tracking of collision-free waypoint paths produced by an offline planner for a planar double-integrator system with bounded speed and acceleration. Because sampling-based planners must route around obstacles, the resulting waypoint paths can contain sharp turns and high-curvature regions, so one-step reachability under acceleration limits becomes critical even when the path geometry is collision-free. We build on a pure-pursuit-style, reachability-guided quadratic-program (QP) tracker with a one-step acceleration margin. Offline, we evaluate this margin along a spline fitted to the waypoint path and update a scalar speed-scaling profile so that the required one-step acceleration remains below the available bound. Online, the same look-ahead tracking structure is used to track the scaled reference.

AI.tldr: This paper studies tracking of collision-free waypoint paths for planar double-integrator systems with bounded speed and acceleration. It builds on a pure-pursuit-style, reachability-guided QP tracker with a one-step acceleration margin, updating a speed-scaling profile offline to ensure acceleration constraints are satisfied during online tracking.
AI.motivation: Sampling-based planners route around obstacles, producing waypoint paths with sharp turns and high-curvature regions. One-step reachability under acceleration limits becomes critical even when path geometry is collision-free.
AI.method: Build on a pure-pursuit-style, reachability-guided quadratic-program (QP) tracker with a one-step acceleration margin. Offline: evaluate margin along a spline fitted to waypoint path and update a scalar speed-scaling profile. Online: use same look-ahead tracking structure to track scaled reference.
AI.result: The method updates speed-scaling profiles to ensure required one-step acceleration remains below available bounds, enabling safe tracking of collision-free waypoint paths under acceleration constraints.
AI.conclusion: The proposed approach effectively manages acceleration constraints during tracking of waypoint paths generated by offline planners, making it suitable for real-world applications requiring precise motion control.

title: Multi-Camera View Scaling for Data-Efficient Robot Imitation Learning
summary: The generalization ability of imitation learning policies for robotic manipulation is fundamentally constrained by the diversity of expert demonstrations, while collecting demonstrations across varied environments is costly and difficult in practice. In this paper, we propose a practical framework that exploits inherent scene diversity without additional human effort by scaling camera views during demonstration collection. Instead of acquiring more trajectories, multiple synchronized camera perspectives are used to generate pseudo-demonstrations from each expert trajectory, which enriches the training distribution and improves viewpoint invariance in visual representations. We analyze how different action spaces interact with view scaling and show that camera-space representations further enhance diversity. In addition, we introduce a multiview action aggregation method that allows single-view policies to benefit from multiple cameras during deployment. Extensive experiments in simulation and real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate significant gains in data efficiency and generalization compared to single-view baselines. Our results suggest that scaling camera views provides a practical and scalable solution for imitation learning, which requires minimal additional hardware setup and integrates seamlessly with existing imitation learning algorithms. The website of our project is https://yichen928.github.io/robot_multiview.

AI.tldr: A practical framework that scales camera views during demonstration collection to generate pseudo-demonstrations, enriching the training distribution and improving viewpoint invariance without additional human effort or hardware.
AI.motivation: The generalization ability of imitation learning policies for robotic manipulation is fundamentally constrained by the diversity of expert demonstrations. Collecting demonstrations across varied environments is costly and difficult in practice, creating a need to exploit inherent scene diversity without additional human effort.
AI.method: The proposed framework uses multiple synchronized camera perspectives to generate pseudo-demonstrations from each expert trajectory instead of acquiring more trajectories. It analyzes how different action spaces interact with view scaling and introduces a multiview action aggregation method that allows single-view policies to benefit from multiple cameras during deployment. Camera-space representations further enhance diversity.
AI.result: Extensive experiments in simulation and real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate significant gains in data efficiency and generalization compared to single-view baselines. The approach requires minimal additional hardware setup and integrates seamlessly with existing imitation learning algorithms.
AI.conclusion: Scaling camera views provides a practical and scalable solution for imitation learning that enriches the training distribution and improves viewpoint invariance without requiring expensive additional data collection or human effort.

title: A Physical Imitation Learning Pipeline for Energy-Efficient Quadruped Locomotion Assisted by Parallel Elastic Joint
summary: Due to brain-body co-evolution, animals' intrinsic body dynamics play a crucial role in energy-efficient locomotion, which shares control effort between active muscles and passive body dynamics -- a principle known as Embodied Physical Intelligence. In contrast, robot bodies are often designed with one centralised controller that typically suppress the intrinsic body dynamics instead of exploiting it. We introduce Physical Imitation Learning (PIL), which distils a Reinforcement Learning (RL) control policy into physically implementable body responses that can be directly offloaded to passive Parallel Elastic Joints (PEJs), enabling therefore the body to imitate part of the controlled behaviour. Meanwhile, the residual policy commands the motors to recover the RL policy's performance. The results is an overall reduced energy consumption thanks to outsourcing parts of the control policy to the PEJs. Here we show in simulated quadrupeds, that our PIL approach can offloads up to 87% of mechanical power to PEJs on flat terrain and 18% on rough terrain. Because the body design is distilled from -- rather than jointly optimised with -- the control policy, PIL realises brain-body co-design without expanding the search space with body design parameters, providing a computationally efficient route to task-specific Embodied Physical Intelligence applicable to a wide range of joint-based robot morphologies.

AI.tldr: Physical Imitation Learning (PIL) distills RL control policies into passive Parallel Elastic Joint responses that can be offloaded to reduce energy consumption in quadruped locomotion.
AI.motivation: Animals exploit intrinsic body dynamics through brain-body co-evolution for energy-efficient locomotion, whereas robots typically suppress body dynamics with centralized controllers. The authors aim to leverage passive body dynamics to reduce energy consumption in robot locomotion.
AI.method: Physical Imitation Learning (PIL) distills Reinforcement Learning (RL) control policies into physically implementable body responses that can be offloaded to passive Parallel Elastic Joints (PEJs). The residual policy commands motors to recover the RL policy's performance. Body design is distilled from (not jointly optimized with) the control policy.
AI.result: In simulated quadrupeds, PIL offloads up to 87% of mechanical power to PEJs on flat terrain and 18% on rough terrain, achieving overall reduced energy consumption.
AI.conclusion: PIL provides a computationally efficient route to task-specific Embodied Physical Intelligence applicable to various joint-based robot morphologies without expanding the search space with body design parameters.

title: StretchBot: A Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Adaptive Guidance with Assistive Robots
summary: Assistive robots have growing potential to support physical wellbeing in home and healthcare settings, for example, by guiding users through stretching or rehabilitation routines. However, existing systems remain largely scripted, which limits their ability to adapt to user state, environmental context, and interaction dynamics. In this work, we present StretchBot, a hybrid neuro-symbolic robotic coach for adaptive assistive guidance. The system combines multimodal perception with knowledge-graph-grounded large language model reasoning to support context-aware adjustments during short stretching sessions while maintaining a structured routine. To complement the system description, we report an exploratory pilot comparison between scripted and adaptive guidance with three participants. The pilot findings suggest that the adaptive condition improved perceived adaptability and contextual relevance, while scripted guidance remained competitive in smoothness and predictability. These results provide preliminary evidence that structured actionable knowledge can help ground language-model-based adaptation in embodied assistive interaction, while also highlighting the need for larger, longitudinal studies to evaluate robustness, generalizability, and long-term user experience.

AI.tldr: StretchBot is a hybrid neuro-symbolic robotic coach combining multimodal perception with knowledge-graph-grounded LLM reasoning to provide adaptive assistive guidance during stretching sessions. A pilot study with three participants showed that adaptive guidance improved perceived adaptability and contextual relevance compared to scripted guidance, which remained competitive in smoothness and predictability.
AI.motivation: Existing assistive robot systems are largely scripted, limiting their ability to adapt to user state, environmental context, and interaction dynamics in home and healthcare settings.
AI.method: The authors developed StretchBot, a hybrid neuro-symbolic robotic coach that combines multimodal perception with knowledge-graph-grounded large language model reasoning. They conducted an exploratory pilot comparison between scripted and adaptive guidance with three participants.
AI.result: Adaptive guidance improved perceived adaptability and contextual relevance, while scripted guidance remained competitive in smoothness and predictability.
AI.conclusion: Structured actionable knowledge can help ground language-model-based adaptation in embodied assistive interaction, but larger, longitudinal studies are needed to evaluate robustness, generalizability, and long-term user experience.

title: LiPS: Lightweight Panoptic Segmentation for Resource-Constrained Robotics
comment: Submitted to IEEE ICIP 2026. Under review
summary: Panoptic segmentation is a key enabler for robotic perception, as it unifies semantic understanding with object-level reasoning. However, the increasing complexity of state-of-the-art models makes them unsuitable for deployment on resource-constrained platforms such as mobile robots. We propose a novel approach called LiPS that addresses the challenge of efficient-to-compute panoptic segmentation with a lightweight design that retains query-based decoding while introducing a streamlined feature extraction and fusion pathway. It aims at providing a strong panoptic segmentation performance while substantially lowering the computational demands. Evaluations on standard benchmarks demonstrate that LiPS attains accuracy comparable to much heavier baselines, while providing up to 4.5 higher throughput, measured in frames per second, and requiring nearly 6.8 times fewer computations. This efficiency makes LiPS a highly relevant bridge between modern panoptic models and real-world robotic applications.

AI.tldr: LiPS is a lightweight panoptic segmentation approach that maintains query-based decoding while streamlining feature extraction and fusion pathways, achieving comparable accuracy to heavier baselines with significantly lower computational demands.
AI.motivation: Panoptic segmentation is crucial for robotic perception as it unifies semantic understanding with object-level reasoning. However, state-of-the-art models have become too complex for deployment on resource-constrained platforms such as mobile robots.
AI.method: LiPS introduces a lightweight design that retains query-based decoding while introducing a streamlined feature extraction and fusion pathway to reduce computational demands.
AI.result: LiPS achieves accuracy comparable to much heavier baselines, with up to 4.5x higher throughput (frames per second) and nearly 6.8x fewer computations required.
AI.conclusion: LiPS serves as an efficient bridge between modern panoptic models and real-world robotic applications, making panoptic segmentation viable for resource-constrained deployment scenarios.

title: SoftHand Model-W: A 3D-Printed, Anthropomorphic, Underactuated Robot Hand with Integrated Wrist and Carpal Tunnel
comment: Accepted for publication at the International Conference of Robotics and Automation (ICRA) 2026, Vienna
summary: This paper presents the SoftHand Model-W: a 3D-printed, underactuated, anthropomorphic robot hand based on the Pisa/IIT SoftHand, with an integrated antagonistic tendon mechanism and 2 degree-of-freedom tendon-driven wrist. These four degrees-of-acuation provide active flexion and extension to the five fingers, and active flexion/extension and radial/ulnar deviation of the palm through the wrist, while preserving the synergistic and self-adaptive features of such SoftHands. A carpal tunnel-inspired tendon routing allows remote motor placement in the forearm, reducing distal inertia and maintaining a compact form factor. The SoftHand-W is mounted on a 6-axis robot arm and tested with two reorientation tasks requiring coordination between the hand and arm's pose: cube stacking and in-plane disc rotation. Results comparing task time, arm joint travel, and configuration changes with and without wrist actuation show that adding the wrist reduces compensatory and reconfiguration movements of the arm for a quicker task-completion time. Moreover, the wrist enables pick-and-place operations that would be impossible otherwise. Overall, the SoftHand Model-W demonstrates how proximal degrees of freedom are key to achieving versatile, human-like manipulation in real world robotic applications, with a compact design enabling deployment in research and assistive settings.

AI.tldr: A 3D-printed, underactuated anthropomorphic robot hand (SoftHand Model-W) with an integrated antagonistic tendon mechanism and 2-DOF wrist, demonstrating that proximal degrees of freedom significantly enhance versatile manipulation capabilities.
AI.motivation: Create a versatile, human-like manipulation system with compact design for real-world robotic applications and assistive settings, exploring how proximal degrees of freedom (wrist actuation) contribute to manipulation versatility.
AI.method: Developed SoftHand Model-W based on Pisa/IIT SoftHand with: 3D-printed underactuated anthropomorphic design, integrated antagonistic tendon mechanism, 2-DOF tendon-driven wrist, carpal tunnel-inspired tendon routing for remote motor placement, mounted on 6-axis robot arm. Tested with cube stacking and in-plane disc rotation tasks.
AI.result: Wrist actuation reduces compensatory and reconfiguration movements of the arm, decreases task completion time, and enables pick-and-place operations that would be impossible without wrist actuation.
AI.conclusion: Proximal degrees of freedom are key to achieving versatile, human-like manipulation in real-world robotic applications; the compact SoftHand Model-W design enables deployment in research and assistive settings.

title: How to Train your Tactile Model: Tactile Perception with Multi-fingered Robot Hands
comment: Accepted for publication at the International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA) 2026, Vienna
summary: Rapid deployment of new tactile sensors is essential for scalable robotic manipulation, especially in multi-fingered hands equipped with vision-based tactile sensors. However, current methods for inferring contact properties rely heavily on convolutional neural networks (CNNs), which, while effective on known sensors, require large, sensor-specific datasets. Furthermore, they require retraining for each new sensor due to differences in lens properties, illumination, and sensor wear. Here we introduce TacViT, a novel tactile perception model based on Vision Transformers, designed to generalize on new sensor data. TacViT leverages global self-attention mechanisms to extract robust features from tactile images, enabling accurate contact property inference even on previously unseen sensors. This capability significantly reduces the need for data collection and retraining, accelerating the deployment of new sensors. We evaluate TacViT on sensors for a five-fingered robot hand and demonstrate its superior generalization performance compared to CNNs. Our results highlight TacViTs potential to make tactile sensing more scalable and practical for real-world robotic applications.

AI.tldr: TacViT is a Vision Transformer-based tactile perception model that generalizes to new sensors without retraining, outperforming CNNs in contact property inference.
AI.motivation: Current tactile perception methods rely heavily on CNNs, which require large sensor-specific datasets and retraining for each new sensor due to differences in lens properties, illumination, and sensor wear. Rapid deployment of new tactile sensors is essential for scalable robotic manipulation.
AI.method: TacViT introduces a Vision Transformer-based architecture with global self-attention mechanisms to extract robust features from tactile images, designed to generalize across different sensors without retraining.
AI.result: Evaluated on sensors for a five-fingered robot hand, TacViT demonstrated superior generalization performance compared to CNNs, enabling accurate contact property inference on previously unseen sensors with significantly reduced data collection and retraining needs.
AI.conclusion: TacViT has the potential to make tactile sensing more scalable and practical for real-world robotic applications by reducing data requirements and enabling faster sensor deployment.

title: A wearable haptic device for edge and surface simulation
summary: Object manipulation is fundamental to virtual reality (VR) applications, yet conventional fingertip haptic devices fail to render certain tactile features relevant for immersive and precise interactions, as i.e. detection of edges. This paper presents a compact, lightweight fingertip haptic device (24.3 g) that delivers distinguishable surface and edge contact feedback through a novel dual-motor mechanism. Pressure distribution characterization using a 6 x 6 flexible sensor array demonstrates distinct contact patterns between the two stimulation modes. A preliminary user study with five participants achieved 93% average classification accuracy across four conditions (edge/surface contact with light/heavy pressure), with mean response times of 2.79 seconds. The results indicate that the proposed device can effectively convey edge and surface tactile cues, potentially enhancing object manipulation fidelity in VR environments.

AI.tldr: A compact 24.3g fingertip haptic device using a novel dual-motor mechanism delivers distinguishable surface and edge contact feedback for VR applications, achieving 93% classification accuracy in detecting edge/surface contact with light/heavy pressure.
AI.motivation: Conventional fingertip haptic devices fail to render certain tactile features relevant for immersive and precise VR interactions, such as edge detection.
AI.method: Developed a lightweight (24.3g) fingertip device with a novel dual-motor mechanism; characterized pressure distribution using a 6x6 flexible sensor array; conducted a preliminary user study with five participants across four conditions (edge/surface contact with light/heavy pressure).
AI.result: Achieved 93% average classification accuracy with mean response times of 2.79 seconds; demonstrated distinct contact patterns between the two stimulation modes.
AI.conclusion: The device effectively conveys edge and surface tactile cues, potentially enhancing object manipulation fidelity in VR environments.

title: A Dual-Action Fabric-Based Soft Robotic Glove for Ergonomic Hand Rehabilitation
summary: Hand impairment following neurological disorders substantially limits independence in activities of daily living, motivating the development of effective assistive and rehabilitation strategies. Soft robotic gloves have attracted growing interest in this context, yet persistent challenges in customization, ergonomic fit, and flexion-extension actuation constrain their clinical utility. Here, we present a dual-action fabric-based soft robotic glove incorporating customized actuators aligned with individual finger joints. The glove comprises five independently controlled dual-action actuators supporting finger flexion and extension, together with a dedicated thumb abduction actuator. Leveraging computer numerical control heat sealing technology, we fabricated symmetrical-chamber actuators that adopt a concave outer surface upon inflation, thereby maximizing finger contact area and improving comfort. Systematic characterization confirmed that the actuators generate sufficient joint moment and fingertip force for ADL-relevant tasks, and that the complete glove system produces adequate grasping force for common household objects. A preliminary study with ten healthy subjects demonstrated that active glove assistance significantly reduces forearm muscle activity during object manipulation. A pilot feasibility study with three individuals with cervical spinal cord injury across seven functional tasks indicated that glove assistance promotes more natural grasp patterns and reduces reliance on tenodesis grasp, although at the cost of increased task completion time attributable to the current actuation interface. This customizable, ergonomic design represents a practical step toward personalized hand rehabilitation and assistive robotics.

AI.tldr: A dual-action fabric-based soft robotic glove with individually controlled actuators for finger flexion/extension and thumb abduction, fabricated via CNC heat sealing for ergonomic fit and comfort. Tested with healthy subjects (reduced muscle activity) and individuals with cervical spinal cord injury (promoted natural grasp patterns).
AI.motivation: Hand impairment from neurological disorders limits ADL independence, while existing soft robotic gloves face challenges in customization, ergonomic fit, and flexion-extension actuation that constrain clinical utility.
AI.method: Developed a glove with five independently controlled dual-action actuators (finger flexion/extension) and a thumb abduction actuator, fabricated using CNC heat sealing to create symmetrical-chamber actuators with concave outer surfaces for improved contact area and comfort.
AI.result: Actuators generate sufficient joint moment and fingertip force for ADL tasks; glove produces adequate grasping force for household objects. Healthy subjects showed reduced forearm muscle activity during manipulation. Cervical SCI participants exhibited more natural grasp patterns with reduced tenodesis reliance, though with increased task completion time.
AI.conclusion: This customizable, ergonomic soft robotic glove design represents a practical step toward personalized hand rehabilitation and assistive robotics.

title: Compact Keyframe-Optimized Multi-Agent Gaussian Splatting SLAM
summary: Efficient multi-agent 3D mapping is essential for robotic teams operating in unknown environments, but dense representations hinder real-time exchange over constrained communication links. In multi-agent Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM), systems typically rely on a centralized server to merge and optimize the local maps produced by individual agents. However, sharing these large map representations, particularly those generated by recent methods such as Gaussian Splatting, becomes a bottleneck in real-world scenarios with limited bandwidth. We present an improved multi-agent RGB-D Gaussian Splatting SLAM framework that reduces communication load while preserving map fidelity. First, we incorporate a compaction step into our SLAM system to remove redundant 3D Gaussians, without degrading the rendering quality. Second, our approach performs centralized loop closure computation without initial guess, operating in two modes: a pure rendered-depth mode that requires no data beyond the 3D Gaussians, and a camera-depth mode that includes lightweight depth images for improved registration accuracy and additional Gaussian pruning. Evaluation on both synthetic and real-world datasets shows up to 85-95\% reduction in transmitted data compared to state-of-the-art approaches in both modes, bringing 3D Gaussian multi-agent SLAM closer to practical deployment in real-world scenarios. Code: https://github.com/lemonci/coko-slam

AI.tldr: An improved multi-agent RGB-D Gaussian Splatting SLAM framework that reduces communication load through Gaussian compaction and efficient centralized loop closure computation, achieving up to 85-95% data reduction compared to state-of-the-art methods.
AI.motivation: Dense map representations (especially from Gaussian Splatting) hinder real-time exchange over constrained communication links in multi-agent SLAM. Centralized server merging of large maps becomes a bottleneck in real-world scenarios with limited bandwidth.
AI.method: 1. Gaussian compaction step to remove redundant 3D Gaussians without degrading rendering quality; 2. Centralized loop closure computation in two modes: (a) pure rendered-depth mode using only 3D Gaussians, (b) camera-depth mode with lightweight depth images for improved registration and additional Gaussian pruning.
AI.result: Up to 85-95% reduction in transmitted data compared to state-of-the-art approaches in both loop closure modes, demonstrating significant communication efficiency gains.
AI.conclusion: The approach successfully reduces communication load while preserving map fidelity, bringing 3D Gaussian multi-agent SLAM closer to practical deployment in real-world scenarios with limited bandwidth.

title: PanoAir: A Panoramic Visual-Inertial SLAM with Cross-Time Real-World UAV Dataset
summary:
Accurate pose estimation is fundamental for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) applications, where Visual-Inertial SLAM (VI-SLAM) provides a cost-effective solution for localization and mapping. However, existing VI-SLAM methods mainly rely on sensors with limited fields of view (FoV), which can lead to drift and even failure in complex UAV scenarios. Although panoramic cameras provide omnidirectional perception to improve robustness, panoramic VI-SLAM and corresponding real-world datasets for UAVs remain underexplored. To address this limitation, we first construct a real-world panoramic visual-inertial dataset covering diverse flight conditions, including varying illumination, altitudes, trajectory lengths, and motion dynamics. To achieve accurate and robust pose estimation under such challenging UAV scenarios, we propose a panoramic VI-SLAM framework that exploits the omnidirectional FoV via the proposed panoramic feature extraction and panoramic loop closure, enhancing feature constraints and ensuring global consistency. Extensive experiments on both the proposed dataset and public benchmarks demonstrate that our method achieves superior accuracy, robustness, and consistency compared to existing approaches. Moreover, deployment on embedded platform validates its practical applicability, achieving comparable computational efficiency to PC implementations.
  The source code and dataset are publicly available at https://drive.google.com/file/d/1lG1Upn6yi-N6tYpEHAt6dfR1uhzNtWbT/view

AI.tldr: A panoramic VI-SLAM framework for UAV pose estimation using omnidirectional perception, with a comprehensive real-world dataset and embedded deployment
AI.motivation: Existing VI-SLAM methods rely on limited field of view (FoV) sensors, causing drift and failure in complex UAV scenarios. Panoramic cameras offer omnidirectional perception but panoramic VI-SLAM and corresponding real-world datasets remain underexplored.
AI.method:
1. Constructed a real-world panoramic visual-inertial dataset covering diverse flight conditions (varying illumination, altitudes, trajectory lengths, motion dynamics)
2. Proposed a panoramic VI-SLAM framework featuring:
   - Panoramic feature extraction
   - Panoramic loop closure
   - Exploitation of omnidirectional FoV to enhance feature constraints and ensure global consistency
3. Deployed on embedded platform for practical applicability
AI.result: Achieved superior accuracy, robustness, and consistency compared to existing approaches on both the proposed dataset and public benchmarks. Deployment on embedded platform demonstrated comparable computational efficiency to PC implementations.
AI.conclusion: The proposed panoramic VI-SLAM framework is practical and effective for UAV applications, with source code and dataset publicly available, demonstrating that omnidirectional perception can significantly improve pose estimation performance in challenging UAV scenarios.

title: An Integrated Soft Robotic System for Measuring Vital Signs in Search and Rescue Environments
summary: Robots are frequently utilized in search-and-rescue operations. In recent years, significant advancements have been made in the field of victim assessment. However, there are still open issues regarding heart rate measurement, and no studies have been found that assess pressure in post-disaster scenarios. This work designs a soft gripper and integrates it into a mobile robotic system, thereby creating a device capable of measuring the pulse and blood pressure of victims in post-disaster environments. The gripper is designed to envelop the victim's arm and inflate like a sphygmomanometer, facilitated by a specialized portability system. The utilization of different signal processing algorithms has enabled the attainment of a pulse bias of \qty{4}{\bpm} and a bias of approximately \qty{5}{\mmHg} for systolic and diastolic pressures. The findings, in conjunction with the other statistical data and the validation of homoscedasticity in the error terms, prove the system's capacity to accurately determine heart rate and blood pressure, thereby rendering it suitable for search and rescue operations. Finally, a post-disaster has been employed as a test to validate the functionality of the entire system and to demonstrate its capacity to adapt to various victim positions, its measurement speed, and its safety for victims.

AI.tldr: A soft gripper integrated into a mobile robotic system for measuring heart rate and blood pressure of victims in post-disaster scenarios, achieving pulse bias of 4 bpm and blood pressure bias of ~5 mmHg.
AI.motivation: Robots are widely used in search-and-rescue operations, but heart rate measurement remains an open issue, and no studies have assessed blood pressure in post-disaster environments.
AI.method: Designs a soft gripper that envelops the victim's arm and inflates like a sphygmomanometer, integrated with a mobile robotic system and specialized portability system; uses different signal processing algorithms.
AI.result: The system achieved a pulse bias of 4 bpm and a bias of approximately 5 mmHg for systolic and diastolic pressures, with statistical validation proving accurate measurement capability.
AI.conclusion: The system is suitable for search and rescue operations; a post-disaster test validated its functionality, adaptability to various victim positions, measurement speed, and safety for victims.

title: Infinite-Horizon Ergodic Control via Kernel Mean Embeddings
summary: This paper derives an infinite-horizon ergodic controller based on kernel mean embeddings for long-duration coverage tasks on general domains. While existing kernel-based ergodic control methods provide strong coverage guarantees on general coverage domains, their practical use has been limited to sub-ergodic, finite-time horizons due to intractable computational scaling, prohibiting its use for long-duration coverage. We resolve this scaling by deriving an infinite-horizon ergodic controller equipped with an extended kernel mean embedding error visitation state that recursively records state visitation. This extended state decouples past visitation from future control synthesis and expands ergodic control to infinite-time settings. In addition, we present a variation of the controller that operates on a receding-horizon control formulation with the extended error state. We demonstrate theoretical proof of asymptotic convergence of the derived controller and show preservation of ergodic coverage guarantees for a class of 2D and 3D coverage problems.

AI.tldr: This paper develops an infinite-horizon ergodic controller based on kernel mean embeddings for long-duration coverage tasks on general domains, solving the computational scaling limitations of existing kernel-based ergodic control methods.
AI.motivation: Existing kernel-based ergodic control methods provide strong coverage guarantees on general domains but are limited to sub-ergodic, finite-time horizons due to intractable computational scaling, preventing their use for long-duration coverage tasks.
AI.method: The authors derive an infinite-horizon ergodic controller equipped with an extended kernel mean embedding error visitation state that recursively records state visitation. This extended state decouples past visitation from future control synthesis and expands ergodic control to infinite-time settings. A receding-horizon variation operating with the extended error state is also presented.
AI.result: The paper provides theoretical proof of asymptotic convergence of the derived controller and demonstrates preservation of ergodic coverage guarantees for a class of 2D and 3D coverage problems.
AI.conclusion: By extending ergodic control to infinite-time settings while maintaining coverage guarantees, the proposed method makes kernel-based ergodic control practical for long-duration coverage tasks on general domains.

title: Stein Variational Uncertainty-Adaptive Model Predictive Control
summary: We propose a Stein variational distributionally robust controller for nonlinear dynamical systems with latent parametric uncertainty. The method is an alternative to conservative worst-case ambiguity-set optimization with a deterministic particle-based approximation of a task-dependent uncertainty distribution, enabling the controller to concentrate on parameter sensitivities that most strongly affect closed-loop performance. Our method yields a controller that is robust to latent parameter uncertainty by coupling optimal control with Stein variational inference, and avoiding restrictive parametric assumptions on the uncertainty model while preserving computational parallelism. In contrast to classical DRO, which can sacrifice nominal performance through worst-case design, we find our approach achieves robustness by shaping the control law around relevant uncertainty that are most critical to the task objective. The proposed framework therefore reconciles robust control and variational inference in a single decision-theoretic formulation for broad classes of control systems with parameter uncertainty. We demonstrate our approach on representative control problems that empirically illustrate improved performance-robustness tradeoffs over nominal, ensemble, and classical distributionally robust baselines.

AI.tldr: A Stein variational distributionally robust controller for nonlinear dynamical systems with latent parametric uncertainty, combining optimal control with Stein variational inference to achieve superior performance-robustness tradeoffs over traditional distributionally robust optimization approaches.
AI.motivation: Latent parameter uncertainty in nonlinear dynamical systems poses significant control challenges. Traditional worst-case ambiguity-set optimization is overly conservative, while classical distributionally robust optimization (DRO) can sacrifice nominal performance. The authors seek to reconcile robust control with variational inference by avoiding restrictive parametric assumptions while preserving computational parallelism.
AI.method: The method couples optimal control with Stein variational inference, employing a particle-based approximation of a task-dependent uncertainty distribution. This approach concentrates on parameter sensitivities that most strongly affect closed-loop performance without requiring restrictive parametric assumptions on the uncertainty model, thereby preserving computational parallelism.
AI.result: The proposed controller demonstrates improved performance-robustness tradeoffs compared to nominal controllers, ensemble methods, and classical distributionally robust baselines on representative control problems. The approach achieves robustness to latent parameter uncertainty by shaping the control law around task-critical uncertainty regions.
AI.conclusion: The framework successfully reconciles robust control and variational inference within a single decision-theoretic formulation for broad classes of control systems with parameter uncertainty, offering a more balanced approach to handling uncertainty than traditional worst-case or distributionally robust methods.

title: BAT: Balancing Agility and Stability via Online Policy Switching for Long-Horizon Whole-Body Humanoid Control
summary: Despite recent advances in control, reinforcement learning, and imitation learning, developing a unified framework that can achieve agile, precise, and robust whole-body behaviors, particularly in long-horizon tasks, remains challenging. Existing approaches typically follow two paradigms: coupled whole-body policies for global coordination and decoupled policies for modular precision. However, without a systematic method to integrate both, this trade-off between agility, robustness, and precision remains unresolved. In this work, we propose BAT, an online policy-switching framework that dynamically selects between two complementary whole-body RL controllers to balance agility and stability across different motion contexts. Our framework consists of two complementary modules: a switching policy learned via hierarchical RL with an expert guidance from sliding-horizon policy pre-evaluation, and an option-aware VQ-VAE that predicts option preference from discrete motion token sequences for improved generalization. The final decision is obtained via confidence-weighted fusion of two modules. Extensive simulations and real-world experiments on the Unitree G1 humanoid robot demonstrate that BAT enables versatile long-horizon loco-manipulation and outperforms prior methods across diverse tasks.

AI.tldr: BAT is an online policy-switching framework that dynamically balances agility and stability in whole-body robotic control for long-horizon tasks by fusing two complementary RL controllers.
AI.motivation: Developing a unified framework for agile, precise, and robust whole-body behaviors in long-horizon tasks remains challenging. Existing approaches face a trade-off between agility (coupled policies) and stability (decoupled policies).
AI.method: BAT consists of two complementary modules: (1) a switching policy learned via hierarchical RL with sliding-horizon policy pre-evaluation for expert guidance, and (2) an option-aware VQ-VAE that predicts option preference from discrete motion token sequences. Final decisions use confidence-weighted fusion of both modules.
AI.result: BAT enables versatile long-horizon loco-manipulation tasks, outperforming prior methods across diverse tasks in both simulation and real-world experiments on the Unitree G1 humanoid robot.
AI.conclusion: Extensive simulations and real-world experiments demonstrate that BAT effectively balances agility and stability, providing a promising solution to the trade-off problem in whole-body robotic control.

title: VRUD: A Drone Dataset for Complex Vehicle-VRU Interactions within Mixed Traffic
summary: The Operational Design Domain (ODD) of urbanoriented Level 4 (L4) autonomous driving, especially for autonomous robotaxis, confronts formidable challenges in complex urban mixed traffic environments. These challenges stem mainly from the high density of Vulnerable Road Users (VRUs) and their highly uncertain and unpredictable interaction behaviors. However, existing open-source datasets predominantly focus on structured scenarios such as highways or regulated intersections, leaving a critical gap in data representing chaotic, unstructured urban environments. To address this, this paper proposes an efficient, high-precision method for constructing drone-based datasets and establishes the Vehicle-Vulnerable Road User Interaction Dataset (VRUD), as illustrated in Figure 1. Distinct from prior works, VRUD is collected from typical "Urban Villages" in Shenzhen, characterized by loose traffic supervision and extreme occlusion. The dataset comprises 4 hours of 4K/30Hz recording, containing 11,479 VRU trajectories and 1,939 vehicle trajectories. A key characteristic of VRUD is its composition: VRUs account for about 87% of all traffic participants, significantly exceeding the proportions in existing benchmarks. Furthermore, unlike datasets that only provide raw trajectories, we extracted 4,002 multi-agent interaction scenarios based on a novel Vector Time to Collision (VTTC) threshold, supported by standard OpenDRIVE HD maps. This study provides valuable, rare edge-case resources for enhancing the safety performance of ADS in complex, unstructured urban environments. To facilitate further research, we have made the VRUD dataset open-source at: https://zzi4.github.io/VRUD/.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces the Vehicle-Vulnerable Road User Interaction Dataset (VRUD), a high-precision drone-based dataset collected from chaotic "Urban Villages" in Shenzhen to address the lack of data for unstructured urban traffic environments in L4 autonomous driving research.
AI.motivation: Urban-oriented Level 4 autonomous driving faces challenges in complex mixed traffic environments with high-density Vulnerable Road Users (VRUs) and unpredictable interaction behaviors. Existing open-source datasets primarily focus on structured scenarios (highways, regulated intersections), leaving a critical gap in data representing chaotic, unstructured urban environments, particularly for edge-case research.
AI.method: The researchers developed an efficient, high-precision drone-based data collection method and constructed the Vehicle-Vulnerable Road User Interaction Dataset (VRUD) from typical "Urban Villages" in Shenzhen, characterized by loose traffic supervision and extreme occlusion. They utilized a novel Vector Time to Collision (VTTC) threshold to extract 4,002 multi-agent interaction scenarios from raw trajectories, supported by standard OpenDRIVE HD maps.
AI.result: The VRUD dataset contains 4 hours of 4K/30Hz recording with 11,479 VRU trajectories and 1,939 vehicle trajectories. Key characteristics include: (1) VRUs account for approximately 87% of all traffic participants (significantly higher than existing benchmarks), (2) 4,002 multi-agent interaction scenarios extracted via VTTC threshold, and (3) comprehensive coverage of chaotic, unstructured urban environments with extreme occlusion.
AI.conclusion: VRUD provides valuable, rare edge-case resources for enhancing the safety performance of autonomous driving systems (ADS) in complex, unstructured urban environments. The dataset has been made open-source at https://zzi4.github.io/VRUD/ to facilitate further research.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Robotic Manipulation under Distribution Shift with Bounded Extremum Seeking
summary: Reinforcement learning has shown strong performance in robotic manipulation, but learned policies often degrade in performance when test conditions differ from the training distribution. This limitation is especially important in contact-rich tasks such as pushing and pick-and-place, where changes in goals, contact conditions, or robot dynamics can drive the system out-of-distribution at inference time. In this paper, we investigate a hybrid controller that combines reinforcement learning with bounded extremum seeking to improve robustness under such conditions. In the proposed approach, deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) policies are trained under standard conditions on the robotic pushing and pick-and-place tasks, and are then combined with bounded ES during deployment. The RL policy provides fast manipulation behavior, while bounded ES ensures robustness of the overall controller to time variations when operating conditions depart from those seen during training. The resulting controller is evaluated under several out-of-distribution settings, including time-varying goals and spatially varying friction patches.

AI.tldr: A hybrid controller combining deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) reinforcement learning with bounded extremum seeking for robust robotic manipulation in contact-rich tasks like pushing and pick-and-place.
AI.motivation: Reinforcement learning policies often degrade when test conditions differ from training distribution, especially in contact-rich tasks where changes in goals, contact conditions, or robot dynamics can drive the system out-of-distribution at inference time.
AI.method: Trains DDPG policies under standard conditions on robotic pushing and pick-and-place tasks, then combines them with bounded extremum seeking during deployment. The RL policy provides fast manipulation behavior while bounded ES ensures robustness to time variations when operating conditions depart from training.
AI.result: The hybrid controller is evaluated under several out-of-distribution settings, including time-varying goals and spatially varying friction patches.
AI.conclusion: The combination of RL with bounded ES provides improved robustness under varying conditions while maintaining fast manipulation capabilities, addressing the out-of-distribution problem in contact-rich robotic tasks.

title: SMASH: Mastering Scalable Whole-Body Skills for Humanoid Ping-Pong with Egocentric Vision
summary: Existing humanoid table tennis systems remain limited by their reliance on external sensing and their inability to achieve agile whole-body coordination for precise task execution. These limitations stem from two core challenges: achieving low-latency and robust onboard egocentric perception under fast robot motion, and obtaining sufficiently diverse task-aligned strike motions for learning precise yet natural whole-body behaviors. In this work, we present \methodname, a modular system for agile humanoid table tennis that unifies scalable whole-body skill learning with onboard egocentric perception, eliminating the need for external cameras during deployment. Our work advances prior humanoid table-tennis systems in three key aspects. First, we achieve agile and precise ball interaction with tightly coordinated whole-body control, rather than relying on decoupled upper- and lower-body behaviors. This enables the system to exhibit diverse strike motions, including explosive whole-body smashes and low crouching shots. Second, by augmenting and diversifying strike motions with a generative model, our framework benefits from scalable motion priors and produces natural, robust striking behaviors across a wide workspace. Third, to the best of our knowledge, we demonstrate the first humanoid table-tennis system capable of consecutive strikes using onboard sensing alone, despite the challenges of low-latency perception, ego-motion-induced instability, and limited field of view. Extensive real-world experiments demonstrate stable and precise ball exchanges under high-speed conditions, validating scalable, perception-driven whole-body skill learning for dynamic humanoid interaction tasks.

AI.tldr: A modular humanoid table tennis system that achieves agile whole-body coordination and consecutive strikes using only onboard egocentric perception, eliminating the need for external cameras.
AI.motivation: Existing humanoid table tennis systems are limited by their reliance on external sensing and inability to achieve agile whole-body coordination. Two core challenges: (1) achieving low-latency and robust onboard egocentric perception under fast robot motion, and (2) obtaining sufficiently diverse task-aligned strike motions for learning precise yet natural whole-body behaviors.
AI.method: \methodname, a modular system that unifies scalable whole-body skill learning with onboard egocentric perception. It uses a generative model to augment and diversify strike motions, producing natural, robust striking behaviors. The system eliminates external cameras during deployment.
AI.result: Achieves agile and precise ball interaction with tightly coordinated whole-body control, enabling diverse strike motions including explosive smashes and low crouching shots. Demonstrates the first humanoid table tennis system capable of consecutive strikes using onboard sensing alone, despite challenges of low-latency perception, ego-motion-induced instability, and limited field of view.
AI.conclusion: Extensive real-world experiments validate stable and precise ball exchanges under high-speed conditions, demonstrating the feasibility of scalable, perception-driven whole-body skill learning for dynamic humanoid interaction tasks.

title: Functional Force-Aware Retargeting from Virtual Human Demos to Soft Robot Policies
summary: We introduce SoftAct, a framework for teaching soft robot hands to perform human-like manipulation skills by explicitly reasoning about contact forces. Leveraging immersive virtual reality, our system captures rich human demonstrations, including hand kinematics, object motion, dense contact patches, and detailed contact force information. Unlike conventional approaches that retarget human joint trajectories, SoftAct employs a two-stage, force-aware retargeting algorithm. The first stage attributes demonstrated contact forces to individual human fingers and allocates robot fingers proportionally, establishing a force-balanced mapping between human and robot hands. The second stage performs online retargeting by combining baseline end-effector pose tracking with geodesic-weighted contact refinements, using contact geometry and force magnitude to adjust robot fingertip targets in real time. This formulation enables soft robotic hands to reproduce the functional intent of human demonstrations while naturally accommodating extreme embodiment mismatch and nonlinear compliance. We evaluate SoftAct on a suite of contact-rich manipulation tasks using a custom non-anthropomorphic pneumatic soft robot hand. SoftAct's controller reduces fingertip trajectory tracking RMSE by up to 55 percent and reduces tracking variance by up to 69 percent compared to kinematic and learning-based baselines. At the policy level, SoftAct achieves consistently higher success in zero-shot real-world deployment and in simulation. These results demonstrate that explicitly modeling contact geometry and force distribution is essential for effective skill transfer to soft robotic hands, and cannot be recovered through kinematic imitation alone. Project videos and additional details are available at https://soft-act.github.io/.

AI.tldr: SoftAct is a force-aware retargeting framework that uses immersive VR to capture human demonstrations and transfers them to soft robot hands via a two-stage algorithm combining force-balanced mapping with geodesic-weighted contact refinements, enabling effective skill transfer despite extreme embodiment mismatch.
AI.motivation: Conventional kinematic retargeting fails to transfer skills to soft robot hands due to extreme embodiment mismatch and nonlinear compliance; explicitly modeling contact geometry and force distribution is essential for effective skill transfer, which cannot be recovered through kinematic imitation alone.
AI.method: 1) Captures rich human demonstrations in VR including kinematics, object motion, dense contact patches, and contact forces. 2) Two-stage force-aware retargeting: Stage 1 attributes demonstrated contact forces to individual fingers and allocates robot fingers proportionally to establish force-balanced mapping; Stage 2 performs online retargeting combining baseline end-effector pose tracking with geodesic-weighted contact refinements, adjusting robot fingertip targets in real-time using contact geometry and force magnitude.
AI.result: Evaluated on contact-rich tasks with a non-anthropomorphic pneumatic soft robot hand. Reduces fingertip trajectory tracking RMSE by up to 55% and tracking variance by up to 69% compared to kinematic and learning-based baselines. Achieves consistently higher success rates in zero-shot real-world deployment and simulation.
AI.conclusion: Explicitly modeling contact geometry and force distribution is essential for effective skill transfer to soft robotic hands. SoftAct enables soft robot hands to reproduce the functional intent of human demonstrations while naturally accommodating extreme embodiment mismatch and nonlinear compliance, demonstrating that force-aware approaches outperform kinematic imitation alone.
